stories.title: Mumbai airport will lose about a quarter of its capacity from next winter
stories.summary: Mumbai airport's two terminals handled 55 million passengers last fiscal, but by October 2027 it will handle only 40 million, a 27 per cent drop, as Terminal 1 shuts for redevelopment, the Times of India reports. It will stay smaller until December 2030 or later.

stories.title: Mumbai airport asks airlines for Terminal 1 transition plans by November 3
stories.summary: Mumbai International Airport Limited has asked the Airline Operators Committee, which represents 47 airlines, to submit transition and slot relocation plans by November 3 for Terminal 1's redevelopment, a project delayed for more than nine years, the New Indian Express reports.

stories.title: IndiGo now flies the world's longest A321XLR route
stories.summary: IndiGo has begun flying the single aisle Airbus A321XLR on its 11 hour Mumbai to Amsterdam service, about 6,865 km and the longest A321XLR route per Cirium data, Aerospace Global News reports. It replaced a Boeing 787-9 leased from Norse Atlantic Airways on 25 October.

stories.title: Consumer court orders Air India Express to pay after denying boarding to a mother and child
stories.summary: Aswathy Radhakrishnan and her son, about three, were denied boarding on a confirmed Kochi to Abu Dhabi flight in February 2021. A consumer commission ordered Air India Express to refund the fare and pay Rs 40,000 for mental agony and Rs 10,000 in costs, the Economic Times reports.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh's Rs 300 crore jet waits for DGCA clearance
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh's newly purchased Bombardier Challenger 3500, which cost over Rs 300 crore, landed in Bhopal on October 19 and is parked in the state hangar awaiting DGCA flying permission, likely by end November or early December, the Free Press Journal reports.

stories.title: Why planes circle before landing
stories.summary: When a plane circles within sight of the airport, it is often simply waiting its turn to land, Mathrubhumi explains. Such delays mean extra fuel burn, higher airline costs and more emissions, and better coordination of arrivals can reduce them, the piece argues.

stories.title: Eurocontrol expects 110,000 fewer European flights this year
stories.summary: Middle East conflicts are expected to cost European aviation around 110,000 flights in 2026, Eurocontrol forecasts, with flights in the ECAC region growing 1.7 per cent to 11.2 million instead of the projected 2.7 per cent, Anadolu reports. It expects 3.2 per cent growth in 2027.

stories.title: WestJet faces $1.6 billion more a year in fuel costs
stories.summary: WestJet CEO Alexis von Hoensbroech told the Calgary Chamber of Commerce the airline faces an additional $1.6 billion in annual fuel costs, and told CityNews fares will eventually have to reflect it. 'People will have to expect that airlines will eventually have to recover the cost of fuel,' he said.

stories.title: Scott Kirby wants United to be America's Emirates
stories.summary: United CEO Scott Kirby told The Dallas Morning News he wants United to be a brand all Americans are proud of, comparing the ambition to the standing of Emirates and Singapore Airlines at home, Simple Flying reports. He says there is plenty of room for improvement first.

stories.title: Frontier ends flights to 21 airports while growing overall
stories.summary: Frontier Airlines will average 644 daily movements from November to early April, up 7 per cent on a year earlier, largely as it backfills capacity left by the now defunct Spirit Airlines, Simple Flying reports. It has still ended all flights to 21 airports.

stories.title: Jet2 says its all business class 737 is selling well
stories.summary: UK leisure carrier Jet2.com says its first business class configured Boeing 737-800, converted from 189 economy seats to 76 seats in a 2-2 layout, has had a strong positive reaction from the market, Aviation Week reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: ITA Airways and Archer plan air taxis into Italian city centres
stories.summary: ITA Airways has become the first European carrier to join Archer Aviation's partner network, with plans for electric air taxi links between Italian airports and city centres, Business Traveller reports. Certification and launch dates remain unresolved. Rome in 10 minutes, eventually.

stories.title: Emirates moves all its Vietnam flights to the A350
stories.summary: Emirates will add a second daily A350 service between Dubai and Ho Chi Minh City from November 1, and put the A350 on both daily Hanoi services from December 1, so all four daily Vietnam flights use the aircraft, AeroTime reports.

stories.title: Icelandair picks Toronto and New York for its first A320neo transatlantic routes
stories.summary: Icelandair will fly its incoming Airbus A320neos from Keflavik to Toronto and New York, six times weekly each, from September 2027, according to schedules published by AeroRoutes, Simple Flying reports. The airline is retiring its remaining passenger 757s and 767s.

stories.title: Philippine Airlines puts the A350-1000 on San Francisco daily
stories.summary: Philippine Airlines is now flying its flagship Airbus A350-1000 daily between Manila and San Francisco ahead of the year end peak, when many Filipino Americans fly home for the holidays, AeroTime reports. San Francisco is one of its most important North American gateways.

stories.title: United will leave Tulum after less than two years
stories.summary: United Airlines will end both its Tulum routes, with the year round Houston service ending January 2 and seasonal Newark flights ending January 24, Simple Flying reports. United began serving Tulum in April 2024.

stories.title: Discover Airlines will take over Lufthansa's Costa Rica route
stories.summary: Lufthansa will stop flying to Costa Rica after December 13, 2027, and sister airline Discover Airlines will take over the Frankfurt to San José route the next day, raising service from five to six weekly flights on A350-900s, the Tico Times reports.

stories.title: Alaska Airlines takes its sixth 787-9
stories.summary: Alaska Airlines has taken delivery of its sixth Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, which left Boeing's Charleston facility for Los Angeles, Simple Flying reports. Another 11 are on order, and the airline is preparing more European services in 2027 as its long haul push grows after buying Hawaiian Airlines.

stories.title: Air cargo demand rose in September as passenger numbers fell
stories.summary: IATA data shows global airfreight demand grew for a second month in a row in September while passenger figures dropped, FlightGlobal reports. The full piece, including the numbers, is for subscribers. Boxes, it seems, are travelling more than people.

stories.title: Starlux and Etihad frequent flyer deal now works both ways
stories.summary: From 28 October, Starlux's Cosmile members can earn and redeem miles on Etihad, and Etihad Guest members, who could already spend miles on Starlux since August, can now collect them on the Taiwanese carrier, Business Traveller reports.

stories.title: Aviation Capital Group orders 75 A320neo family jets
stories.summary: California based lessor Aviation Capital Group has signed a firm order for 75 Airbus A320neo family aircraft, the largest in its nearly 40 year history, taking its total A320neo family orders to 190, the Leader reports. Their wings are made at Airbus's Broughton factory in Flintshire.

stories.title: Boeing's CEO says production will scale up right, not fast
stories.summary: Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said after third quarter results that stabilising 737 MAX production is taking longer than expected. 'I know everybody wants us to go faster, but we're going to do it right,' he said, Live From A Lounge reports.

stories.title: A supplier dispute has halted Boeing's 777 freighter line
stories.summary: Boeing's 777F production has been halted for almost two months after a dispute with Florida supplier Vaero over wing rib kits, and had not resumed as of 23 October despite a September settlement, Reuters reported, Tribune Online notes. The 767 line was affected too.

stories.title: Boeing forecasts more than 4,000 freighters by 2045
stories.summary: Boeing's 2026 World Air Cargo Forecast projects air cargo traffic will double over 20 years, needing nearly 3,000 new and converted freighters and lifting the global fleet past 4,000 by 2045, Avionews reports. It cites advanced manufacturing, AI hardware and ecommerce.

stories.title: FAA issues a first special certificate to BETA's electric aircraft
stories.summary: The FAA has issued a first of its kind Special Airworthiness Market Survey Certificate to BETA Technologies, allowing its ALIA A250 eVTOL to fly with operators and participants for market surveys and to operate in more environments, the AASHTO Journal reports.

stories.title: Boeing and Lufthansa Technik extend their parts deal
stories.summary: Boeing and Lufthansa Technik have extended their Tailored Parts Package agreement by three years at MRO Europe in Amsterdam, giving access to more than 6,500 Boeing part numbers across its commercial aircraft platforms, AeroTime reports.

stories.title: AerCap leases two converted 777 freighters to Turkish Airlines
stories.summary: AerCap has signed lease agreements with Turkish Airlines for two Boeing 777-300ERSF converted freighters, with deliveries between March and September 2027, PR Newswire reports. The conversions will take place at Etihad Engineering's MRO hub in Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: US air medical operators order eight Airbus helicopters
stories.summary: Boston MedFlight has ordered three Airbus H145s and Life Flight Network five H135s for emergency medical missions, AvioRadar reports. Boston MedFlight's latest order takes its total H145 purchases over time to 12.

stories.title: JetZero gets $5.3 million from the FAA
stories.summary: JetZero has received a $5.3 million award from the Federal Aviation Administration, its latest round of federal funding, to track engine environmental impact data, the Greensboro News and Record reports. The rest of the article did not load for us.

stories.title: Gulfstream's parent sees no barrier to 200 deliveries a year
stories.summary: Gulfstream's parent says the airframer has the capacity to reach 200 deliveries a year by 2030, but further rate increases would require additional investment, FlightGlobal reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: I Squared Capital buys aerostructures supplier Orizon
stories.summary: Private equity firm I Squared Capital is acquiring Orizon Aerostructures, a key supplier to aircraft makers and large defence primes, according to managing partner and chief investment officer Gautam Bhandari, Aviation Week reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Six killed in Uttarakhand helicopter crash near Joshimath
stories.summary: A helicopter carrying pilgrims returning from Badrinath Dham crashed in remote mountains near Joshimath on Friday, killing all six on board including the pilot. The AAIB will examine the wreckage, flight data and cockpit voice recorder, and whether weather, visibility, a fault or overloading contributed, the New Indian Express reports.

stories.title: Three killed as two helicopters collide near an Oregon airport
stories.summary: A Robinson R22 and an Airbus H125 collided near McMinnville Municipal Airport on Thursday afternoon, killing all three people aboard, Fox News reports. They included 22 year old flight instructor Maddie Aasbo, a student pilot from the UK and Tyler Delane Sturdevant, 38.

stories.title: FAA proposes a $2.4 million fine against a California flight school
stories.summary: The FAA proposed a $2,388,500 penalty against Stratus Aviation, which runs Wings Flight School in Vacaville, alleging an unapproved temperature gauge installed in 2022 made a Cessna 172M unairworthy for about 280 flights, AVweb reports. No resulting accidents or injuries were identified.

stories.title: Atlanta controllers switch from paper strips to electronic ones
stories.summary: Air traffic controllers at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport began using electronic flight strips this week, replacing paper strips used for decades, the FAA said, Fox 5 Atlanta reports. The system gives real time flight information and alerts controllers to changes such as runway closures.

stories.title: FAA hunts for faster ways to find radio interference
stories.summary: The FAA wants equipment that can pinpoint sources of interference across the 30,000 radio frequencies aviation uses, since current methods can take weeks, AvBrief reports. Officials said the existing approach 'was designed for a quieter world in the aviation spectrum that no longer exists.'

stories.title: Reliable Robotics tests an uncrewed Cessna Caravan for cargo
stories.summary: Autonomous flight startup Reliable Robotics has begun test flights from Albuquerque with a Cessna Caravan modified into an uncrewed aircraft, aiming at revenue cargo flights under an FAA advanced air mobility pilot project, Aviation Week reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: UK consults on rejoining EGNOS satellite positioning
stories.summary: The UK Department for Transport has launched a consultation on rejoining EGNOS, the European satellite based augmentation system that improves positioning accuracy, which the UK lost access to after Brexit, Aviation Week reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Denver hangar tenants drop lawsuit after FAA backs an 82 per cent rent rise
stories.summary: Tenants at Centennial Airport in Denver dropped their lawsuit against Denver jetCenter after the FAA upheld its 82 per cent hangar rent increase, from $660 to $1,200 a month for a T-hangar, which took effect in April, AOPA reports.

stories.title: Michigan airport drops its light aircraft landing fees
stories.summary: Manistee County Blacker Airport in Michigan has replaced its new weight based landing fees, which started at $10 for aircraft under 6,000 pounds, with charges tied to ramp parking and landside access, AVweb reports. Aircraft that skip those services can land without the fee.

stories.title: Synapse Aviation launches a flight briefing tool for threat and error management
stories.summary: Synapse Aviation has launched Adaptive TEM, a tool aimed at the manual work of pulling weather, NOTAMs, terrain charts and runway limits into crews' threat and error management briefings, AeroTime reports. Some threats, it notes, are otherwise found only when workload is already high.

stories.title: Air India gets DGCA approval for a 34 aircraft flying academy
stories.summary: Air India has received DGCA approval to run a flying academy at Belora Airport in Amravati, Maharashtra, with 31 single engine and three twin engine aircraft on 10 acres, CNBC TV18 reports. It will be India's first flying academy set up by an Indian airline.

stories.title: Why the FAA ended single pilot exemptions on about 1,250 Citations
stories.summary: After two fatal single pilot Cessna Citation crashes in 2025, an FAA audit found 13 of 14 training providers out of compliance, and it ended 40 years of solo pilot exemptions for legacy Citations on September 29, Simple Flying reports. The business aviation lobby pushed back.

stories.title: Helicopter Institute will train NASA astronauts to fly helicopters
stories.summary: Helicopter Institute has been selected by NASA to train astronauts and pilots at its Fort Worth facility to fly US Navy TH-57 helicopters recently transferred to the agency, RotorHub reports. In the 1960s NASA used Bell 47s to help astronauts train for lunar landings.

stories.title: FAA Mobile Clearance will let pilots request IFR clearances by app
stories.summary: By early 2027, the FAA's Mobile Clearance tool will let general and business aviation pilots request IFR departure clearances and cancellations through apps such as ForeFlight and Garmin, moving from voice to text to reduce readback errors, Flying reports.

stories.title: Europe prepares to change how air traffic controllers are trained
stories.summary: EASA and Eurocontrol held a workshop on 27 and 28 October to prepare regulators for an amendment to EU ATCO licensing rules that will introduce competency based training and assessment for controllers from 1 January 2029, The Aviation Hub reports.

stories.title: Kentucky college opens an aviation maintenance programme
stories.summary: West Kentucky Community and Technical College marked the launch of its new Aviation Maintenance Technology programme with an FAA certificate unveiling and ribbon cutting in Paducah on October 30, funded by $2.3 million from the Kentucky legislature, Marshall County Daily reports. It prepares students to inspect, maintain and repair aircraft.

research.title: A Community Impact-Centered Network Reduction Method for Power Systems Resilience Planning
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Power systems resilience planning requires evaluating many hazard scenarios and investment portfolios, often requiring network reduction for computational tractability. The resulting aggregation, however, can obscure community impact data needed for equitable planning. We present a network. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This study introduces a new approach for building surrogate models, in the form of Reduced Order Models (ROMs), for PDE-constrained optimization. A physics-constrained data-driven framework is developed to transform large-scale non-linear optimization problems into ROM-constrained optimization. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Optimal Seed Reveals the Dynamical Route to Spontaneous Splitting of Turbulent Puffs
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: The localized turbulence in pipe flow, known as puffs, is sustained by their proliferation. This process is crucial to the subcritical laminar-turbulent transition, a century-old fundamental problem related to a wide range of natural and engineered. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: BEVLight: Generalizable Traffic Signal Control from UAV Bird's-Eye Views
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based traffic signal control (TSC) has achieved promising performance, but most methods rely on structured traffic states that must be estimated from sensor observations in real deployments. Visual TSC learns signal decisions directly from images, yet. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Belief-Driven Search in Connectivity-Constrained Mobile Sensor Networks with Convergence Guarantees
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent search and coverage is critical to autonomous exploration, search-and-rescue, and defense applications. This paper investigates settings where a mobile sensor network is tasked with coordinating to discover the position of a stationary target within a. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Causality-informed dynamic mode decomposition for unsteady flow analysis
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Causal analysis characterizes directional dependencies in dynamical systems, while such information is not typically used to inform reduced-order modeling of unsteady flows. This study proposes a Granger Causality-informed Dynamic Mode Decomposition (GC-DMD) framework that incorporates such. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Compound Climate Risk-Aware Electricity Dispatch: Trajectory-Based Modeling for Power System Resilience
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent decades, emerging compound hazards in a changing climate have increasingly threatened power system resilience and posed new challenges to electricity dispatch. Conventional Value-at-Risk (VaR)-based risk-aware dispatch provides a tractable means of managing stochastic net. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Computationally Constrained First-Order Prediction-Correction Approach for Time-Varying Convex Optimization
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying optimization methods often predict the locations of time-varying optima, then sample the objective function being minimized, and then compute corrections to those predictions. However, those works typically do not account for settings in which computations. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
